rubric.evidence: IDL transcribed from the WICG spec of 4 March 2026 (fetched 2026-09-13), with the spec's bikeshed markup artifact on the autofillValues member lines removed and that removal disclosed on the page. The upgrade corrected two factual errors in the previous revision: the event fires AT THE DOCUMENT (spec 4.1 'Dispatch event at document'), not on individual input/select/textarea controls, and it fires BEFORE values are committed (the autofill operation runs immediately after dispatch), not 'after the browser completes autofill'. Spec/explainer drift (bubbles=true + autofillValues/DOMString in the spec vs non-bubbling + values/string|boolean in the explainer) is disclosed rather than papered over. Refill rejection paths, the retry-with-null-refill rule, and the full-address token are transcribed from spec sections 3.1, 4.2, and 5.

Slug autofill-event is the slugified milestone-listing name 'Autofill event'; the feature appears in the milestone=147 listing's features_by_type under 'Origin trial' with id 5137581018841088 (verified by direct API query 2026-09-13). The Intent to Experiment confirms origin trial milestones 147-152 on desktop and Android. The chromestatus identity link is unchanged from the previous revision.

reference-contract.json inventories the full spec surface (event, constructor, autofillValues, refill, RefillCallback, AutofillEventInit, AutofillValueEntry, full-address token); autofillValues and refill have dedicated child routes with all rejection paths, null conditions, entry-shape caveats, and state transitions; the rest is covered by nine-dimension doc-tables on the overview. deno task validate-artifacts passes for this feature.

why-it-exists explains the dynamic-address-form problem, the hidden-field workaround and its abuse, and the announce->adapt->refill loop, sourced to spec section 1 and the explainer. The refill lifecycle is presented as an explicit state-transition table. Not yet explained: why the spec chose bubbles=true when the event targets the document (no public rationale found to cite).

Overview carries the spec's canonical US-state checkout example (condensed, with the refill error path added), a document-level logging example, and a synthetic-event example for third-party providers; child pages add value-snapshot and double-call-guard patterns. The live showcase refill-flow demo is embedded (HEAD 200, 2026-09-13) and the owner's two demo pages are linked (both 200). Not runtime-executed by this writer: no Chrome 147 with stored autofill profile data is available in this environment, so behavior is source-derived, not observed.

Honest interim tables on all three pages: Chrome desktop+Android 147-152 origin trial (Intent to Experiment + listing), Android WebView divergence quoted from the ChromeStatus record ('don't yet support autofill retriggering'), Edge not available with the absence of an announcement stated as unlinkable, Firefox/Safari 'no signal' each linked to their open standards-position issues. BCD absence (no api/AutofillEvent.json, no autofill_event key in api/Document.json) and webstatus.dev zero-match query both checked 2026-09-13 and linked. MDN non-coverage stated with the search-API link; page explicitly remains a full reference, not a stub.

Every external URL on the three pages was checked 2026-09-13: spec, chromestatus feature + milestone listing, both blink-dev intent threads (subjects verified: Intent to Prototype 2026-01-14, Intent to Experiment 2026-02-19 with LGTM), OT registration page, runtime_enabled_features.json5, tracking bug, WICG repo + proposals#162, TAG review #1197, mozilla#1361, WebKit#431, webdriver-bidi#706, both yoavweiss demos, webstatus query, MDN search API and :autofill page, WebIDL/DOM/HTML spec anchors, showcase feature + refill-flow routes (GitHub pages verified via authenticated fetch because the build proxy 403s anonymous github.com requests). The previous revision's two unlinked citation labels ('chromestatus motivation', 'standards positions') now link directly.

Semantic tables with th scope=row, baseline banner with role=note and aria-label, single h1 with h2/h3 hierarchy, iframe with a descriptive title attribute, wbr in the long child-page h1. Follows the accepted exemplar's patterns (v152/window-shape-api); not separately audited with a screen reader.

css-layout guidance applied: .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto} around every table, overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1/lede/code/td, pre{overflow-x:auto}, baseline-browsers flex-wrap, iframe max-width:100% with loading=lazy and fixed height (no CLS even if the embed is slow). CDP-measured at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 on all three routes (2026-09-13): documentElement.scrollWidth === innerWidth everywhere (360/360, 1280/1280), zero console errors; screenshots READ at both viewports (banner, doc-tables, pre blocks all contained and legible). The only failed requests were external (fonts.googleapis.com and the showcase iframe origin), which this sandbox's egress blocks for the browser — out of gendn's scope per the conformance runner's same-origin-only network-failure rule.

Embedded the refill-flow concept route (HEAD 200 via proxy, 2026-09-13); the showcase feature index and its other concept routes (autofill-log, autofill-vs-input, compatibility-lab, formdata-autofill-tester) also 200, and the route is served with no X-Frame-Options and only a report-only CSP, so framing is permitted. The showcase feature page links back to this gendn route; see-also links the showcase feature index. Caveat: the iframe's visual render could NOT be confirmed in this sandbox — headless Chrome's external HTTPS is blocked at the egress (ERR_CONNECTION_RESET for the showcase origin AND fonts.googleapis.com; relay log shows the tunnel killed mid-TLS-handshake), so the embed shows blank in local screenshots. This is an environment artifact, not a page defect; flagged for integrator re-verification from an unrestricted environment.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation tables without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on intrinsic sizing; wrap potentially-wide content in overflow containers; overflow-wrap on unbreakable tokens; flex-wrap for wrapping rows.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: every doc/compat table sits in .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto}; overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1, lede, code and table cells; <wbr> in the long autofillValues child h1; baseline-browsers list uses flex with wrap; pre blocks scroll internally. Exception: no container queries — the shared single-column editorial measure fits the reference format (same as the accepted v152 exemplar).

guidanceConsulted.query: embedding third-party iframe demo lazy loading performance
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Defer below-the-fold embeds with loading=lazy so they do not compete with critical resources; never lazy-load the LCP element.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: the showcase demo iframe sits far below the fold in the Examples section and carries loading="lazy" with explicit width/height (no CLS); the LCP element (lede text) is plain HTML and unaffected.

openQuestions: The spec initializes bubbles=true for an event dispatched at the Document (nothing above it to bubble to except the window via the document tree), while the explainer says the event does not bubble; no public rationale for the flag choice was found. Re-check the spec after the origin trial and update the event-flags row if this changes.

The spec's rendered IDL block (and IDL Index) contains a bikeshed markup artifact leaking href/id attribute text into the autofillValues member lines (observed 2026-09-13). The page reproduces the IDL with the artifact removed and discloses that. If WICG fixes the build, drop the transcription note.

AutofillValueEntry is typed sequence<any> with the tuple shape given only in an IDL comment; whether Chrome's implementation enforces [HTMLElement, DOMString] pairs on synthetic AutofillEventInit.autofillValues entries is not specified and was not runtime-verified.

Whether Chrome exposes the AutofillEvent constructor without the OT token (interface exposure vs event firing) was not runtime-verified; the pages conservatively say the interface exists only with the trial/flag enabled.

The embedded showcase refill-flow iframe renders blank in this sandbox because the egress blocks headless Chrome's external HTTPS entirely (fonts fail the same way); the route is 200 and frameable per its headers. An integrator with unrestricted egress should confirm the embed paints on mobile and desktop.
